BCF STARsolo workflow

How to apply it on different scRNA-Seq technologies

Author

Florian Geier (florian.geier@unibas.ch), Igor Cervenka (igor.cervenka@unibas.ch)

Published

October 13, 2026

Snakemake

  • Snakemake is a python based workflow tool

  • If you are new to Snakemake take a look at our tutorial

BCF workflows

  • The Bioinformatics Core Facility (BCF) maintains a collection of Snakemake workflows for recurring analyses (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq mapping) in the sciCORE GitLab:

    https://git.scicore.unibas.ch/DBM_bioinfo/ivanek/snakemake/workflows

  • All workflows follow the same layout recommended in the Snakemake best practices: the workflow code lives in workflow/, the configuration in config/ and the results are written to results/ next to them.

How to get them?

  • The repositories are not public. Contact the BCF with your sciCORE/GitLab user name to get access to the project.

  • Once you have access, clone a specific workflow into your project folder (not your home, the workflow produces a lot of data!). Each analysis gets its own clone of the workflow:

cd /scicore/projects/<my_project>/
## via ssh (requires a ssh key registered in GitLab)
git clone -b public_dev ssh://git@git.scicore.unibas.ch:2222/DBM_bioinfo/ivanek/snakemake/workflows/starsolo_mapping_workflow.git
## or via https
git clone -b public_dev https://git.scicore.unibas.ch/DBM_bioinfo/ivanek/snakemake/workflows/starsolo_mapping_workflow.git
cd starsolo_mapping_workflow
Tip

Record the exact version of the workflow you used, e.g. with git rev-parse HEAD or by checking out a tagged release (git checkout <tag>). Together with the conda environments this makes your mapping reproducible.

Repository structure

starsolo_mapping_workflow/
├── config/
│   ├── defaults.yaml        # default tool settings - don't change
│   └── config.yaml          # YOUR project configuration (to be created)
├── docs/                    # detailed documentation (markdown)
├── schemas/                 # validation of config, sample sheet and hashtag file
├── workflow/
│   ├── Snakefile            # main entry point, rule `all`
│   ├── rules/*.smk          # rules grouped by step
│   ├── scripts/             # R and python scripts called by the rules
│   └── envs/*.yaml          # conda environment per tool
└── README.md
Important

Always run Snakemake from the root of the repository (the folder containing config/ and workflow/). Scripts and configuration files are referenced relative to it.

STARsolo workflow

  • The workflow maps single-cell RNA-seq (and related) reads with STARsolo, quantifies UMIs per cell barcode and gene, removes empty droplets and returns one SingleCellExperiment (SCE) object for all samples of a project, together with QC reports.

  • STARsolo is a drop-in replacement for Cell Ranger, but:

    • It is considerably faster and open source
    • The barcode/UMI geometry is fully configurable, i.e. it is not restricted to 10x Genomics protocols
    • Several count types (exonic, full gene body, spliced/unspliced) can be produced in one run

  • On top of STARsolo, the workflow adds steps that are needed in most of our projects:

    • Additional read pre-processing capabilities
    • cell hashing and antibody (CITE-seq) quantification
    • sample demultiplexing by hashtags, sample barcodes or genotypes (SNPs)
    • detection of empty droplets
    • joining all samples into one SingleCellExperiment object

  • Downstream analysis like dimensionality reduction, clustering or cell type annotation isn’t part of the workflow, but we provide a notebook template for these steps operating on SingleCellExperiment objects

Features

The workflow runs the following steps (optional steps are only executed when configured):

# Step Rule(s) Output folder
1 Build genome reference and STAR index (if not provided) process_references, STAR_index resources/<genome>/
2 (optional) cDNA read trimming with fastp (ADT/HTO) trim_cDNA results/trim_cDNA_<stype>/
3 (optional) read pre-processing (BD Rhapsody, 10x Flex) process_paired_reads results/process_paired_reads_<stype>/
4 Alignment, barcode/UMI correction and counting with STARsolo STARsolo, STARsolo_altmod results/STARsolo/<sample>/<stype>/
5 Mapping and counting QC across samples STARsolo_qc, samtools_* results/STARsolo/
6 Create one unfiltered SCE per sample (all assays, ADT/HTO, sample annotation) create_sce results/create_sce/<sample>/
7 Empty droplet removal empty_droplets results/empty_drops/<sample>/
8 (optional) sample demultiplexing by HTO demultiplex_HTO results/demultiplex_HTO/<sample>/
9 (optional) donor demultiplexing by SNPs get_barcodes_eSNP, cellsnp_lite, vireo, cluster_genotypes results/demultiplex_SNP/
10 Join all samples into one SCE + QC join_sce, joined_sce_qc results/join_sce/
  • <stype> is the sequence type of a library (GEX, ADT, HTO, ADT+HTO), see Assays.
  • <sample> is the SampleName from the sample sheet, <tag> the output_tag from the config file.

Assays

The workflow can quantify several read types (assays) per sample. The assay of a library is given in the SequenceType column of the sample sheet:

Assay SequenceType Description Ends up in the SCE as
Gene expression GEX the transcriptome, mapped to the genome (or 10x Flex probe set) main assays (counts, …)
Antibody-derived tags (CITE-seq) ADT surface protein quantification with oligo-tagged antibodies altExp(sce, "ADT")
Cell hashing HTO oligo-tagged antibodies/lipids used to label cells of different samples before pooling altExp(sce, "HTO")
ADT and HTO in one library ADT+HTO both are sequenced from the same FASTQ files and split after counting altExp(sce, "ADT"), altExp(sce, "HTO")
  • ADT and HTO libraries are called alternative modalities (altmods). Their reads are mapped to a small index built from the tag sequences listed in a hashtag file, using the same cell barcodes as the GEX library.

In addition, pooled samples can be demultiplexed in different ways:

Demultiplexing by When How Result column(s) in colData(sce)
Hashtags (HTO) cell hashing (e.g. TotalSeq hashtag antibodies) DropletUtils::hashedDrops() DemuxSampleNameHTO
Genotype (SNP) pooled samples from different (human) donors cellSNP-lite + vireo DemuxSNP, DemuxSampleNameSNP
Sample barcodes 10x Flex, Parse Biosciences, 10x on-chip multiplexing sample barcode is part of the barcode read SampleBarcodeLabel, DemuxSampleNameSB
  • HTO demultiplexing is activated automatically as soon as HTO sequences are present in the hashtag file.
  • SNP demultiplexing has to be switched on in the config (demultiplex_SNP: active: True).
  • sample barcodes are configured via barcodes: samples.

Technologies

Each library preparation protocol has its own barcode/UMI geometry, which has to be translated into STARsolo options:

Protocol STARsolo mode Special handling Docs
10x Genomics 3’ v2/v3/v3.1/v4 (GEM-X) CB_UMI_Simple whitelist depends on chemistry docs/technologies/10x-3prime.md
10x Genomics Flex (v1, v2) / APEX CB_UMI_Complex probe set reference, sample barcodes, read pre-processing (FLEX) docs/technologies/10x-flex.md
BD Rhapsody (Enhanced V2 beads) CB_UMI_Complex 3 cell barcode segments separated by linkers docs/technologies/bd-rhapsody.md
Parse Biosciences (split-pool) CB_UMI_Complex read 1/2 swapped, polyT/random hexamer merging, sample barcodes docs/technologies/parse-biosciences.md
BRB-seq (bulk, multiplexed) CB_UMI_Simple no empty droplet removal docs/technologies/brb-seq.md
  • CB_UMI_Simple: cell barcode (CB) and UMI are at fixed positions of the barcode read (e.g. 10x: CB = bases 1-16, UMI = bases 17-28).
  • CB_UMI_Complex: CB consists of several segments, each with its own whitelist, and positions can be anchored to an adapter sequence instead of the read start. This is the template for any protocol not listed here, see the STARsolo docs on complex barcodes.

Configuration

The final configuration is assembled from several layers. Later layers overwrite earlier ones:

  1. config/defaults.yaml: default tool settings (STARsolo options, empty droplet removal, demultiplexing). Don’t change it.
  2. config/config.yaml: your project configuration: required options plus any default you want to overwrite (e.g. technology specific STARsolo geometry).
  3. Sample sheet and hashtag file: parsed into the config (samples, fastq_files, hashtags).

  • What you put into config.yaml therefore depends on the technology (barcode geometry, whitelist, read processing) and the assays (ADT/HTO, demultiplexing) of your experiment, see the examples below.

  • The fully resolved configuration is written to logs/starsolo_mapping_config.yaml on every run. Check this file first if a setting doesn’t seem to take effect.

Documentation

  • The detailed documentation is part of the repository (docs/) and can be read directly in GitLab (markdown files are rendered there) or in any text editor:
Section File(s) Content
Quick start README.md workflow steps, minimal config, how to run, cleaning up
Index docs/home.md links to all pages
Configuration docs/configuration.md, docs/configuration/*.md config.yaml vs defaults.yaml, sample sheet, genome annotation, cell barcodes & sample barcodes
Assays docs/assays.md, docs/assays/*.md gene expression options (features, multimappers, empty droplets), ADT/HTO, SNP demultiplexing
Technologies docs/technologies.md, docs/technologies/*.md example configs for 10x 3’, 10x Flex, BD Rhapsody, Parse, BRB-seq

  • Recommended reading order: README.md → docs/configuration.md → the page of your technology → the pages of your assays.

  • The docs are also set up as a MkDocs site, which you can browse locally:

pip install mkdocs
mkdocs serve # open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser
  • The STARsolo options themselves are documented in the STARsolo docs and the STAR manual.

How to configure

To run the workflow you need (at least) two files:

  • sample sheet
  • config file (config/config.yaml).

Experiments with ADT/HTO libraries additionally need a hashtag file.

Sample sheet

  • The sample sheet is a tab-separated file listing all FASTQ files, one row per read pair (i.e. per sequencing lane/run):
Column Required Description
FileName1 yes barcode read (R1 for 10x)
FileName2 yes cDNA read (R2 for 10x)
SampleName yes sample identifier (e.g. sequencing facility ID GFB_xxxx)
SampleGroup yes sample group/condition
ExternalSampleName recommended human readable sample name, used in QC plots
SequenceType for ADT/HTO GEX (default if missing), ADT, HTO or ADT+HTO

  • Rows with the same SampleName (and SequenceType) are mapped together, i.e. multiple lanes/flowcells of one library are combined automatically.

  • FASTQ paths can be absolute or relative to the location of the sample sheet.

  • All other columns are copied into the cell annotation (colData) of the SCE object. This is a convenient way to add sample annotation (e.g. Genotype, Treatment, Donor).

Creating the sample sheet from the sequencing facility data

  • For data sequenced by the Genomics Facility Basel (GFB) the script flowcell2samples.py collects the FASTQ files and their metadata from the openBIS userstore (/scicore/projects/openbis/userstore/):
python scripts/flowcell2samples.py <FLOWCELL_ID> [<FLOWCELL_ID_2> ...] -g <group> -o samples.txt
# e.g. <group> = dbm_<groupname> or biozentrum_<groupname>
  • The output contains the columns FileName1, FileName2, FileSizeGB1, FileSizeGB2, SampleName, ExternalSampleName, FlowcellID, SampleType, Kit, NCycles, Species, ContactPerson. It has to be cleaned up and SampleGroup has to be added, e.g. in R:
make_sample_sheet.R
sf <- read.delim("samples.txt", header = TRUE, quote = '"')
sf$SampleGroup <- "ctrl" # add the real grouping here
# keep only columns that are constant per sample
sf <- sf[, c("FileName1", "FileName2", "SampleName", "ExternalSampleName", "SampleGroup")]
write.table(sf, file = "samples.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
  • Alternatively, write the sample sheet by hand (or with a few lines of bash/python) for data from other sources.
Note
  • flowcell2samples.py puts R1 into FileName1. For protocols where the barcode is in read 2 (e.g. Parse Biosciences) the two columns need to be swapped.
  • Alternatively, one change change read order in the workflow by overriding the defaults
config.yaml
read_order:
  barcode: 1 # 0 = R1 by default
  cDNA: 0 # 1 = R2 by default
  • The sample names from the facility (GFB-1234) are converted to GFB_1234 by the script.

Hashtag file

  • Only needed if the experiment contains ADT and/or HTO libraries. Tab-separated with the columns Sequence, SequenceName and SequenceType (ADT or HTO):
hashtags.tsv
Sequence    SequenceName    SequenceType
GTCAACTCTTTAGCG hashtag1    HTO
TGATGGCCTATTGGG hashtag2    HTO
AAACTCAGGTCCTTC CD34    ADT
CAACGCCTAGAAACC CD150   ADT
  • The file is referenced in the config with hashtag_file: hashtags.tsv.
  • The sequences are used to build a small STAR index, i.e. the cDNA read (after optional trimming) is aligned against them.
  • If not all HTOs were used in every sample, restrict them per sample (an empty list disables HTO demultiplexing for that sample):
config.yaml
hto_per_sample:
  GFB_1001: ['hashtag1', 'hashtag2']
  GFB_1002: []
  • HTO demultiplexing runs automatically for all samples with HTOs. Thresholds for doublet calling can be changed:
config.yaml
demultiplex_HTO:
  doublet_nmads: 3       # LogFC2 must be doublet_nmads MADs above the median
  doublet_min: 2         # AND LogFC2 greater than doublet_min
  doublet_mixture: False # alternatively: 2-component mixture model
  • Results: colData(sce)$DemuxSampleNameHTO (<SampleName>_<hashtag>, NA for doublets and unassigned cells) and the detailed hashedDrops() output in colData(altExp(sce, "HTO"))$DemuxHTO. The QC report is results/demultiplex_HTO/<tag>_qc.pdf.

Config file

The user configuration lives at config/config.yaml. The required options are:

Option Description
output_tag prefix for output file names, e.g. hg38_ensdb112 (genome + annotation is a good choice)
sample_file path to the sample sheet
genome genome sequence/STAR index and gene annotation
barcodes cell barcode whitelist(s), optionally feature barcode translation and sample barcodes

Genome and annotation

  • Use a pre-built STAR index together with its GTF file:
config.yaml
genome:
  hg38:
    index: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_genomes/hg38/STAR
    gtf: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_annotations/hg38/hg38_ensdb112_toUCSC_filtered.gtf
  • … or let the workflow build the index from a FASTA file (written to resources/<genome>/):
config.yaml
genome:
  hg38:
    fasta: <path/to/hg38.fa>
    gtf: <path/to/hg38.gtf>
    chrom_in_use: [chr1, chr2, ...] # optional: subset, e.g. without haplotypes and unplaced contigs
  • Further options (see docs/configuration/genome-annotation.md):
    • Extra sequences (transgenes, vectors, viruses): add a second entry with its own FASTA; gtf: whole_contig counts the whole contig as one gene
    • Competitive mapping (e.g. human xenograft in mouse): add the background genome without gtf. Chromosome/contig names of additional references are appended by the genome name + underscore in order to avoid chromosome/contig name collisions (hg38, mm11_chr1)
    • 10x Flex probe set: build a small reference from the probe set CSV (probe_set:), see Example 5
Note

A pre-built index must be compatible with the STAR version of the workflow (see workflow/envs/STAR.yaml).

Cell barcodes

  • All barcode files go into the barcodes: block. Files can be used as provided by the vendor (gzipped, several columns, header line): the workflow extracts the barcodes to results/barcodes/<stype>/.
config.yaml
barcodes:
  whitelist: <file or list of files>  # required, one file per cell barcode segment
  translation: <file>                 # optional, ADT/HTO with 10x v3 + TotalSeq B/C
  samples:                            # optional, sample barcodes
    format: flex                      # flex | parse | lists
    file: <file>
  • Where to find whitelists:
Technology Whitelist Location
10x various technologies Cell Ranger (use recent version): lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/
BD Rhapsody 3 files (CLS1-3), see Example 4 BD cell label script
Parse bc_data_*.csv Parse pipeline: splitpipe/barcodes/
  • Cell Ranger installations on sciCORE: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-<version>/. List the available whitelists with:
ls /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-10.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/
  • Settings under barcodes: apply to all sequence types. A block named after a sequence type (GEX, ADT, HTO, ADT+HTO) overrides them for that type only (e.g. a different sample barcode file for a Flex antibody library).

STARsolo options

  • STARsolo command line options are set per sequence type in STARsolo_<stype> blocks, without the leading --:
config.yaml
STARsolo_GEX:
  soloFeatures: GeneFull Gene SJ Velocyto # first feature = primary assay counts(sce)
  soloStrand: Reverse
  clipAdapterType: False                  # False removes a default option

  • Defaults for STARsolo_GEX and for all altmods (STARsolo_altmod, applied to STARsolo_ADT, STARsolo_HTO and STARsolo_ADT+HTO) are listed in config/defaults.yaml.

  • Most important GEX options:

Option Default Meaning
soloType CB_UMI_Simple barcode geometry mode, see Technologies
soloFeatures Gene GeneFull SJ Velocyto count types; the first one becomes counts(sce); SJ is not added to the SCE; Velocyto adds spliced/unspliced assays
soloMultiMappers EM counting of reads mapping to several genes (Unique = only unique reads)
soloStrand Forward read strand relative to the gene (Reverse for 5’ protocols)
soloCBmatchWLtype 1MM_multi_Nbase_pseudocounts barcode error correction (Cell Ranger like)
outFilterMultimapNmax 10 maximum number of loci a read may map to
Note

With the default soloMultiMappers: EM multi-gene reads are distributed fractionally, i.e. the counts are not integers. Set soloMultiMappers: Unique if downstream tools require integer counts.

Empty droplet removal

  • By default DropletUtils::emptyDrops() is used. Droplets with ≤ umi UMIs are considered empty and are used to estimate the ambient RNA profile; droplets above are tested against it:
config.yaml
remove_empty_droplets: empty_drops # alternatively: barcode_ranks (knee point) or cellranger

empty_droplets_options:
  empty_drops:
    umi: 100      # droplets at or below are considered empty
    fdr: 0.001    # FDR threshold to call a cell
  • The QC report (results/empty_drops/<tag>_qc.pdf) shows the knee plot, the p-value distribution of the ambient droplets (should be uniform) and the top ambient genes.

cDNA read trimming for ADT/HTO

  • The cDNA read of ADT/HTO libraries usually contains more than the tag sequence. It is trimmed with fastp before mapping, activated per sequence type (options are passed to fastp as --<option>=<value>):
config.yaml
trim_cDNA_ADT+HTO:
  active: True
  trim_front1: 10 # remove the first 10 bases
  max_len1: 15    # then keep 15 bases (= tag length)

Running the workflow

Dry-run and DAG

  • Always start with a dry-run. It validates the config and sample sheet and shows which jobs would be executed:
cd starsolo_mapping_workflow
conda activate snakemake_9
snakemake -n
  • Visualize the workflow:
snakemake --rulegraph | dot -Tpdf > rulegraph.pdf # rules only
snakemake --dag | dot -Tpdf > dag.pdf             # all jobs (large for many samples!)

Create the conda environments

  • Cluster nodes don’t have internet access, therefore the conda environments have to be created first (on the login node). Using a shared --conda-prefix allows to reuse the environments across projects:
snakemake --sdm conda --conda-create-envs-only --conda-prefix ~/snakemake_environments

Run Snakemake on sciCORE slurm cluster

  • We provide a sciCORE-specific slurm profile at https://git.scicore.unibas.ch/DBM_bioinfo/ivanek/snakemake/profiles/scicore-slurm.git. It offers a few sciCORE specific tweaks:

    • translate time to scicore-slurm qos settings
    • allow setting of group accounts
    • easy to extend to user needs

  • All rules of the workflow define their resources (threads, memory, time), scaled with the input size, so no further adjustments are needed.

  • When installed under $HOME/.config/snakemake, Snakemake can be invoked using the profile:

snakemake --profile scicore-slurm --sdm conda --conda-prefix ~/snakemake_environments
Tip
  • A full run takes several hours. Start Snakemake inside a screen or tmux session on the login node, so that it keeps running when you log out.
  • Add --keep-going to continue with independent jobs when one job fails.
  • You can request intermediate targets, e.g. map all samples and check the mapping QC before the rest of the workflow is run:
snakemake --profile scicore-slurm --sdm conda --conda-prefix ~/snakemake_environments \
  results/STARsolo/GEX_mapping_counting_stats.pdf

Logs and troubleshooting

  • logs/starsolo_mapping_config.yaml: the resolved configuration
  • logs/<rule>/...: one log file per job, e.g. logs/STARsolo/<sample>_GEX.log
  • results/STARsolo/<sample>/<stype>/Log.final.out: STAR mapping statistics
  • results/STARsolo/<sample>/<stype>/Solo.out/<feature>/Summary.csv: barcode and counting statistics
Symptom Likely cause
low Reads With Valid Barcodes in Summary.csv wrong whitelist (chemistry), wrong barcode geometry or swapped FileName1/FileName2
good genome mapping but low Reads Mapped to Gene wrong soloStrand (Forward ↔︎ Reverse)
error in create_sce about duplicated row names sample sheet columns that differ between rows of one sample
setting has no effect typo in option name or wrong block, check logs/starsolo_mapping_config.yaml
STARsolo complains about barcode read length barcode read longer than CB+UMI, set soloBarcodeReadLength: 0
Important

It is not possible to mix samples with ADT/HTO libraries and samples without in one run. Run the workflow separately for each set and join the SCE objects afterwards.

Outputs

results/
├── STARsolo/
│   ├── <sample>/<stype>/                  # BAM (+ bai, flagstats, idxstats), Log.final.out, Solo.out/
│   └── <stype>_mapping_counting_stats.pdf # mapping/counting QC across samples
├── create_sce/<sample>/<tag>_sce.rds      # unfiltered SCE per sample
├── empty_drops/                           # filtered SCE + stats per sample, <tag>_qc.pdf
├── demultiplex_HTO/                       # (optional) <tag>_qc.pdf
├── demultiplex_SNP/                       # (optional) cluster_genotypes.{csv,pdf}
└── join_sce/
    ├── <tag>_sce.rds                      # FINAL OBJECT: all samples, empty droplets removed
    └── <tag>_qc.pdf                       # cells and UMIs per sample
resources/<genome>/                        # genome FASTA/GTF/STAR index (if built by the workflow)
logs/
  • The final object can be loaded in R:
library(SingleCellExperiment)
sce <- readRDS("results/join_sce/hg38_ensdb112_sce.rds")
sce
assayNames(sce)               # e.g. counts (= Gene), GeneFull, spliced, unspliced
metadata(sce)$primary_assay   # which soloFeature is in counts(sce)
altExpNames(sce)              # ADT/HTO if present
table(sce$SampleName)         # cells per sample
head(rowData(sce))            # GENEID, SYMBOL, uniqueSymbol, ... + ambient profile per sample
  • Cell names are <cell barcode>_<sample barcode if present>. The sample sheet columns are found in colData(sce), together with the demultiplexing results (if any).

Cleaning up

  • The workflow produces large intermediate files, roughly 40-50 GB per sample. Once you are happy with the final SCE object remove them with:
snakemake -j 1 clean
Important

clean permanently deletes the per-sample STARsolo results (incl. BAM files), the per-sample SCE objects and the trimmed reads without confirmation. Keep the BAM files if you might need them later (e.g. for genotyping or visualization).

Example 1: 10X v3.1 dataset

  • Human PBMCs, 3’ Gene Expression v3.1, two samples (control and treated), each sequenced on two lanes.
samples.tsv
FileName1   FileName2   SampleName  ExternalSampleName  SampleGroup
fastq/GFB_1001_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_1001_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_1001    PBMC_ctrl   ctrl
fastq/GFB_1001_S1_L002_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_1001_S1_L002_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_1001    PBMC_ctrl   ctrl
fastq/GFB_1002_S2_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_1002_S2_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_1002    PBMC_treat  treat
fastq/GFB_1002_S2_L002_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_1002_S2_L002_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_1002    PBMC_treat  treat
  • The STARsolo defaults correspond to 10x v3/v3.1 (CB 16 bp + UMI 12 bp on read 1), so only the required options are needed:
config/config.yaml
output_tag: hg38_ensdb112
sample_file: samples.tsv

genome:
  hg38:
    index: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_genomes/hg38/STAR
    gtf: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_annotations/hg38/hg38_ensdb112_toUCSC_filtered.gtf

barcodes:
  whitelist: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-7.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/3M-february-2018.txt
Note

If read 1 was sequenced longer than 28 bp, STARsolo refuses the reads unless the length check is switched off and the geometry is given explicitly (see docs/technologies/10x-3prime.md):

config/config.yaml
STARsolo_GEX:
  soloBarcodeReadLength: 0 # don't check length
  soloCBstart: 1
  soloCBlen: 16
  soloUMIstart: 17
  soloUMIlen: 12

Variation: adding CITE-seq antibodies (ADT)

  • Each sample has an additional antibody (TotalSeq B) library. It gets the same SampleName as its GEX library and SequenceType ADT:
samples.tsv
FileName1   FileName2   SampleName  ExternalSampleName  SampleGroup SequenceType
fastq/GFB_1001_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_1001_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_1001    PBMC_ctrl   ctrl    GEX
fastq/GFB_1003_S3_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_1003_S3_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_1001    PBMC_ctrl   ctrl    ADT
fastq/GFB_1002_S2_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_1002_S2_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_1002    PBMC_treat  treat   GEX
fastq/GFB_1004_S4_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_1004_S4_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_1002    PBMC_treat  treat   ADT
  • With v3 chemistry and TotalSeq B/C, the antibody libraries use different cell barcodes than the GEX library, which are translated with the translation file:
config/config.yaml
hashtag_file: hashtags.tsv

barcodes:
  whitelist: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-7.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/3M-february-2018.txt
  translation: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-7.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/translation/3M-february-2018.txt.gz

trim_cDNA_ADT:
  active: True
  trim_front1: 10 # TotalSeq B: 10 bp before the 15 bp antibody barcode
  max_len1: 15
  • The antibody counts are found in altExp(sce, "ADT").

Example 2: 10X v3 dataset with donor demultiplexing

  • Human cells from 4 donors pooled before loading, 3’ Gene Expression v3

  • Donors are identified by their genotype, i.e. by SNPs found in the expressed transcripts. No hashtags are needed.

samples.tsv
FileName1   FileName2   SampleName  ExternalSampleName  SampleGroup
fastq/GFB_2001_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_2001_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_2001    pool_capture1   pool
fastq/GFB_2002_S2_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_2002_S2_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_2002    pool_capture2   pool
config/config.yaml
output_tag: hg38_ensdb112
sample_file: samples.tsv

genome:
  hg38:
    index: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_genomes/hg38/STAR
    gtf: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_annotations/hg38/hg38_ensdb112_toUCSC_filtered.gtf

barcodes:
  whitelist: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-7.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/3M-february-2018.txt

demultiplex_SNP:
  active: True
  vcf: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/genome1K.phase3.SNP_AF5e2.chr1toX.hg38.sorted.ncbi.vcf.bgz
  donors: 4 # number of pooled donors per sample
  • SNP demultiplexing runs per sample (= capture):
    1. Select the n_top_expressed (default 1000) most frequently detected genes, excluding chrY, chrM and genes in the ambient profile
    2. Count reference/alternative alleles of known SNPs (1000 Genomes, allele frequency > 5%) in these genes per cell with cellsnp-lite
    3. Assign cells to donors genotypes with vireo (incl. doublets and unassigned cells)
    4. Cluster the donor genotypes across samples, to identify the same donor in different captures
  • Results: colData(sce)$DemuxSNP (vireo output per cell) and colData(sce)$DemuxSampleNameSNP (donor identity across samples), plus results/demultiplex_SNP/cluster_genotypes.{csv,pdf}.
Important
  • SNP demultiplexing is set up for human data mapped to a genome with UCSC style chromosome names (chr1, chr2, …), with the default empty droplet method (empty_drops), which provides the ambient profile. The chromosome names of the VCF have to match the genome.
  • vireo only tells that cells belong to “donor0”, “donor1”, …: which donor is which person has to be determined from additional information (e.g. sex genes, known genotypes, or a hashtag).

Example 3: 10X with on-chip multiplexing

  • Human cells from 4 donors pooled using on-chip multiplexing, 3’ Gene Expression v4 (GEM-X), two captures of the same pool.
samples.tsv
FileName1   FileName2   SampleName  ExternalSampleName  SampleGroup
fastq/GFB_2001_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_2001_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_2001    pool_capture1   pool
fastq/GFB_2002_S2_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_2002_S2_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_2002    pool_capture2   pool

  • The barcode geometry of v4 is the same as for v3 (CB 16 bp + UMI 12 bp), only the whitelist is different:

  • 4 on-chip barcode lists (OB1-4) identify the 4 donors

  • Files for on-chip multiplexing barcodes need to be downloaded from 10X Website

config/config.yaml
output_tag: hg38_ensdb112
sample_file: samples.tsv

genome:
  hg38:
    index: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_genomes/hg38/STAR
    gtf: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_annotations/hg38/hg38_ensdb112_toUCSC_filtered.gtf

barcodes:
  whitelist: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-10.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/3M-3pgex-may-2023.txt
  samples:
    format: lists
    file:
      OB1: config/ocm_3pgex/OB1_3M-3pgex-may-2023.txt
      OB2: config/ocm_3pgex/OB2_3M-3pgex-may-2023.txt
      OB3: config/ocm_3pgex/OB3_3M-3pgex-may-2023.txt
      OB4: config/ocm_3pgex/OB4_3M-3pgex-may-2023.txt

Example 4: BD Rhapsody dataset

  • 3’ whole transcriptome analysis on BD Rhapsody Enhanced V2 beads, two cartridges (control and treated).

  • The cell barcode consists of 3 segments (CLS1-3, 9 bp each) separated by linkers, preceded by 0-3 random bases:

(N)0-3 - CLS1_9 - GTGA - CLS2_9 - GACA - CLS3_9 - UMI_8 - (T)*
samples.tsv
FileName1   FileName2   SampleName  ExternalSampleName  SampleGroup
fastq/GFB_3001_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_3001_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_3001    cartridge_ctrl  ctrl
fastq/GFB_3002_S2_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_3002_S2_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_3002    cartridge_treat treat

  • Cell barcode whitelists for different BD Rhapsody bead versions can be found in the following script: https://bd-rhapsody-public.s3.amazonaws.com/CellLabel/rhapsody_cell_label.py.txt

  • CLS (cell barcode) whitelists are extracted from the script above and saved as three bd_cls*.csv files, one barcode per line

  • One allowed mismatch per CLS

  • The UMI (8 random bases) directly follows the third CLS

config/config.yaml
output_tag: hg38_ensdb112
sample_file: samples.tsv

genome:
  hg38:
    index: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_genomes/hg38/STAR
    gtf: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_annotations/hg38/hg38_ensdb112_toUCSC_filtered.gtf

barcodes:
  whitelist: [bd_cls1.csv, bd_cls2.csv, bd_cls3.csv]

STARsolo_GEX:
  soloType: CB_UMI_Complex
  soloAdapterSequence: NNNNNNNNNGTGANNNNNNNNNGACA
  soloCBposition: 2_0_2_8 2_13_2_21 3_1_3_9
  soloUMIposition: 3_10_3_17
  soloCBmatchWLtype: 1MM
Note

Alternatively, the barcode read can be pre-processed with the BD read processing (process_paired_reads: active: True, library_type: "BD"), which corrects the CLS segments and outputs a 27 bp cell barcode followed by an 8 bp UMI (STARsolo_GEX: soloCBstart: 1, soloCBlen: 27, soloUMIstart: 28, soloUMIlen: 8). The whitelist is then a single file with all 384³ combinations of CLS1-3, provided by the BCF on sciCORE.

Example 5: Multiplexed Flex v1 dataset

  • Human samples, 10x Flex v1, 4 samples hybridized with different probe barcodes and pooled into one GEM well. The library was sequenced on two lanes in read 1 configuration.
samples.tsv
FileName1   FileName2   SampleName  ExternalSampleName  SampleGroup
fastq/GFB_4001_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_4001_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_4001    flex_pool   all_samples
fastq/GFB_4001_S1_L002_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_4001_S1_L002_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_4001    flex_pool   all_samples
  • Flex specifics:
    • Probe-based: reads are mapped against a small reference built from the probe set (recommended), or against the genome
    • Probe sets need to be download from 10X Website
    • The sample barcode is part of the reads: either at the end of a long read 1 or in read 2, depending on kit version and sequencing configuration
    • We can use read pre-processing (process_paired_reads with library_type: FLEX) detects the sample barcode location and rewrites all reads to CB_16 - UMI_12 - SB_8 (v1; SB_10 for v2) or in the case of read 1 configuration we can specify the positions directly by changing soloCBposition.
    • The sample barcode is treated as an additional cell barcode segment, this file needs to be created by taking the first column of cellranger-10.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/translation/probe-barcodes-fixed-rna-profiling-rna-r1.txt
    • In addition, for sample demultiplexing, the file needs to be included in barcodes/samples, since every sample consists of multiple barcodes that need to be collapsed.
config/config.yaml
output_tag: hg38_flex
sample_file: samples.tsv

genome:
  hg38_flex:
    # Cell Ranger drops probes with included = FALSE, which is default here
    # can be changed by filter_probes: False
    probe_set: <path/to/Chromium_Human_Transcriptome_Probe_Set_v1.1.0_GRCh38-2024-A.csv>

barcodes:
  whitelist: [cellranger-10.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/737K-fixed-rna-profiling.txt, probe-barcodes-fixed-rna-profiling-rna-r1_first_column.txt]
  samples:
    format: flex
    file: cellranger-10.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/translation/probe-barcodes-fixed-rna-profiling-rna-r1.txt

STARsolo_GEX:
  soloType: CB_UMI_Complex
  soloCBposition: 0_0_0_15 0_40_0_47 # cell barcode + sample barcode
  soloUMIposition: "0_16_0_27"       # quoting avoids a parsing issue
  soloCBmatchWLtype: EditDist_2
  clipAdapterType: CellRanger4
  soloFeatures: Gene
  soloStrand: Forward
  soloMultiMappers: Unique
  outFilterMultimapNmax: 1
  alignIntronMax: 1                  # probe set reference only
  • Results: each column of the SCE is a combination of cell barcode and sample barcode. colData(sce)$SampleBarcodeLabel holds the probe barcode label (e.g. BC001) and colData(sce)$DemuxSampleNameSB = <SampleName>_<label>. Annotate the biological samples via a lookup table of the labels downstream.
Important
  • Keep trim_cDNA_GEX inactive: it would cut off a sample barcode sequenced in read 2.
  • With the probe set reference, soloStrand refers to the probe orientation. If hardly any reads are counted (Reads Mapped to Gene in Summary.csv), switch between Forward and Reverse.
  • The location of the sample barcode found by the read pre-processing is written to logs/process_paired_reads/<fqid>_GEX.log.

Tasks for the workshop

  • In each task you get the list of FASTQ files delivered by the sequencing facility, the chemistry used and some information about the experiment.

  • Your task is to prepare everything needed to run the workflow:

    1. Create the sample sheet (samples.tsv)
    2. Create the config file (config/config.yaml)
    3. Find out which additional files are needed and where to get them (e.g. Cell Ranger installation, BD or 10x website, BCF resources on sciCORE), and whether they have to be prepared (e.g. decompressed)

  • Assume that the FASTQ files are located in a folder fastq/ next to the sample sheet. Use the Examples and the workflow documentation (docs/) as reference.

Task 1

  • Chemistry: 10x Genomics GEM-X Single Cell 3’ v4

  • Experiment: human PBMCs from 3 donors were pooled and loaded on two channels of the chip, i.e. two captures (libraries) of the same pool. The donors should be identified by their genotypes. Each library was sequenced on two lanes.

TipSolution
  • The index reads (I1, I2) are not needed. R1 is the barcode read (FileName1), R2 the cDNA read (FileName2). Each lane is one row, rows of the same library share the SampleName:
samples.tsv
FileName1   FileName2   SampleName  ExternalSampleName  SampleGroup
fastq/GFB_5101_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_5101_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_5101    pool_capture1   pool
fastq/GFB_5101_S1_L002_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_5101_S1_L002_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_5101    pool_capture1   pool
fastq/GFB_5102_S2_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_5102_S2_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_5102    pool_capture2   pool
fastq/GFB_5102_S2_L002_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_5102_S2_L002_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_5102    pool_capture2   pool
  • The barcode geometry of v4 (CB 16 bp + UMI 12 bp) is the STARsolo default, only the v4 whitelist has to be set (see Example 3). SNP demultiplexing is activated with the number of pooled donors (see Example 2):
config/config.yaml
output_tag: hg38_ensdb112
sample_file: samples.tsv

genome:
  hg38:
    index: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_genomes/hg38/STAR
    gtf: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/snakemake_annotations/hg38/hg38_ensdb112_toUCSC_filtered.gtf

barcodes:
  whitelist: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-10.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/3M-3pgex-may-2023.txt

demultiplex_SNP:
  active: True
  vcf: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/genome1K.phase3.SNP_AF5e2.chr1toX.hg38.sorted.ncbi.vcf.bgz
  donors: 3
  • Additional files:
File Where to get it
Cell barcode whitelist for 3’ v4 (3M-3pgex-may-2023.txt) Cell Ranger installation: lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/; whitelists have to be uncompressed (gunzip -c <file>.txt.gz > <file>.txt if only a gzipped version is available)
STAR index and GTF (hg38) pre-built by the BCF on sciCORE
SNP file (1000 Genomes, allele frequency > 5%) provided by the BCF on sciCORE (derived from the 1000 Genomes Project)

config/config.yaml

genome:

Alternatively, the barcode read can be pre-processed with the BD read processing (process_paired_reads: active: True, library_type: "BD"), which outputs a 27 bp cell barcode followed by an 8 bp UMI (STARsolo_GEX: soloCBstart: 1, soloCBlen: 27, soloUMIstart: 28, soloUMIlen: 8). The whitelist is then a single file with all 384³ combinations of CLS1-3, provided by the BCF on sciCORE.

Task 3

  • Chemistry: 10x Genomics Flex Gene Expression v1, human, 4-plex

  • Experiment: two libraries (GEM wells), each with 4 samples hybridized with different probe barcodes (BC001-BC004). Each library was sequenced on one lane with read 1 = 28 cycles and read 2 = 90 cycles (sequencing configuration 2).

SampleName ExternalSampleName
GFB_5301 flex_lib1
GFB_5302 flex_lib2
  • Files:
GFB_5301_S1_L001_I1_001.fastq.gz
GFB_5301_S1_L001_I2_001.fastq.gz
GFB_5301_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz
GFB_5301_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz
GFB_5302_S2_L001_I1_001.fastq.gz
GFB_5302_S2_L001_I2_001.fastq.gz
GFB_5302_S2_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz
GFB_5302_S2_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz
  • Compared to Example 5, where is the sample barcode, and what does this mean for the config?
TipSolution
  • One row per library. The samples within a library are separated by their probe barcodes, not by the sample sheet:
samples.tsv
FileName1   FileName2   SampleName  ExternalSampleName  SampleGroup
fastq/GFB_5301_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_5301_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_5301    flex_lib1   all_samples
fastq/GFB_5302_S2_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz  fastq/GFB_5302_S2_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz  GFB_5302    flex_lib2   all_samples
  • With a 28 bp read 1, the sample barcode is not in read 1 but in read 2. The FLEX read processing finds it and rewrites all reads to CB_16 - UMI_12 - SB_8, so the sample barcode is at positions 28-35 of the new barcode read:
config/config.yaml
output_tag: hg38_flex
sample_file: samples.tsv

genome:
  hg38_flex:
    probe_set: <path/to/Chromium_Human_Transcriptome_Probe_Set_v1.1.0_GRCh38-2024-A.csv>

barcodes:
  whitelist: [737K-fixed-rna-profiling.txt, flex_sample_barcodes.txt] # order of soloCBposition
  samples:
    format: flex
    file: /scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-10.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/translation/probe-barcodes-fixed-rna-profiling-rna.txt

process_paired_reads:
  active: True
  library_type: FLEX

STARsolo_GEX:
  soloType: CB_UMI_Complex
  soloCBposition: 0_0_0_15 0_28_0_35 # cell barcode + 8 bp sample barcode (v1)
  soloUMIposition: "0_16_0_27"
  soloCBmatchWLtype: EditDist_2
  clipAdapterType: CellRanger4
  soloFeatures: Gene
  soloBarcodeReadLength: 0
  soloUMIlen: False
  soloStrand: Reverse # check Reads Mapped to Gene in Summary.csv
  soloMultiMappers: Unique
  outFilterMultimapNmax: 1
  alignIntronMax: 1
  • Additional files:
File Where to get it
Cell barcode whitelist (737K-fixed-rna-profiling.txt) Cell Ranger installation: lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/737K-fixed-rna-profiling.txt.gz, decompressed
Probe barcodes (probe-barcodes-fixed-rna-profiling-rna.txt) Cell Ranger installation: lib/python/cellranger/barcodes/translation/; used as is for barcodes: samples
Sample barcode whitelist (flex_sample_barcodes.txt) created from the first column of the probe barcode file
Human probe set CSV 10x website: Cell Ranger probe set downloads 
CR_BARCODES=/scicore/home/ivanek/GROUP/apps/cellranger-10.0.0/lib/python/cellranger/barcodes
gunzip -c $CR_BARCODES/737K-fixed-rna-profiling.txt.gz > 737K-fixed-rna-profiling.txt
grep -v '^#' $CR_BARCODES/translation/probe-barcodes-fixed-rna-profiling-rna.txt | awk '{print $1}' > flex_sample_barcodes.txt
  • The cells are labeled with their probe barcode (SampleBarcodeLabel, e.g. BC001) and DemuxSampleNameSB (e.g. GFB_5301_BC001). The assignment of the probe barcodes to the biological samples is done downstream.
